mechanism: Night solar output is near zero and low-variance, so the most relevant historical analogs are low-level and smooth periods rather than all night windows.
failure_condition: when near dawn/dusk the broad night category mismatches true sun elevation, or when data errors cause non-zero night values
retrieval_action: Prefer same-hour and similar recent_level windows, and prefer windows with similar recent_diff_magnitude, instead of hard-restricting to night only.
expected_effect: Retains night baseline reference while allowing other low-output, low-variability windows to inform the forecast and avoid overfitting night-only segments.
reason: Hard night restriction removed too many analogs; soft same-hour and low-diff matching preserves physically relevant low-output behavior.
claim: Night solar output is near zero and low-variance, so the most relevant historical analogs are low-level and smooth periods rather than all night windows.

mechanism: High recent_diff_magnitude captures active cloud-driven jumps, so short-lag analogs with similar jumpiness are more informative than broad high-volatility windows.
failure_condition: when high recent_diff_magnitude is driven by sunrise/sunset sun-angle changes rather than cloud dynamics, or by data spikes
retrieval_action: Prefer historical windows with similar recent_diff_magnitude and recent_volatility, and use shorter lags to focus on fast cloud dynamics.
expected_effect: Retrieved futures should contain realistic cloud jumps at short horizons and avoid the bias from broad high-volatility windows that dominated negative folds.
reason: Recent jump size is a more specific indicator of cloud-driven variability than volatility alone; short-lag matching focuses on the active cloud regime.
claim: High recent_diff_magnitude captures active cloud-driven jumps, so short-lag analogs with similar jumpiness are more informative than broad high-volatility windows.

mechanism: Morning solar ramp-up creates a steep positive slope; the shape of the ramp depends on sun angle and cloudiness.
activation_condition: when hour_of_day is morning AND recent_slope_magnitude is high
failure_condition: when high slope is due to a cloud edge rather than normal sunrise; when morning ramp is obscured by fog or heavy overcast
retrieval_action: Restrict retrieval to morning history and prefer windows with similar recent_slope_magnitude and recent_level.
expected_effect: Historical morning ramps with similar steepness should provide better forecasts of ramp timing and magnitude over the next hours.
reason: The morning ramp is a semi-deterministic diurnal feature whose slope and level contain information about clear-sky versus cloudy conditions.

notes: retrieval_action subsumed by activation scope; no additional executable transform

claim: Morning solar ramp-up creates a steep positive slope; the shape of the ramp depends on sun angle and cloudiness.

mechanism: Large recent slope magnitude signals an active ramp, and matching ramp strength plus current level captures ramp persistence across all daylight hours.
failure_condition: when the high slope is a transient cloud edge that will leave the horizon, or when slope reverses immediately after the current window
retrieval_action: Prefer historical windows with similar recent_slope_magnitude and recent_level, and use shorter lags instead of restricting retrieval to evening.
expected_effect: Finds ramp-like futures from all hours and avoids the evening-only bias that made the original rule harmful in every fold.
reason: Strong ramps are not confined to evening; slope and level matching provide a more general and trainable ramp regime.
claim: Large recent slope magnitude signals an active ramp, and matching ramp strength plus current level captures ramp persistence across all daylight hours.

mechanism: Low recent_diff_magnitude indicates a stationary clear or overcast state, making operational day-type differences more detectable without being overwhelmed by weather.
failure_condition: when a strong ramp or front is imminent despite low recent diff, or when low diff is only an artifact of night zeros
retrieval_action: Prefer historical windows with similar recent_diff_magnitude and recent_level, and prefer the same working_day, but not restrict by working_day.
expected_effect: Adds a weak day-type signal only in stable regimes, avoiding the harmful non-working-day-only restriction.
reason: Day-type effects are negligible under changing weather; conditioning on low diff magnitude isolates periods where operational differences can matter.
claim: Low recent_diff_magnitude indicates a stationary clear or overcast state, making operational day-type differences more detectable without being overwhelmed by weather.
